leads.name: The Palffy Oak of Memories (Palffyovsky dub spomienok)
leads.why_a_lead: Verify pass 2026-09-27 (Tree of the Year batch 2, target '_tree-of-the-year'). Verifies cleanly on every ordinary test: alive, two-plus independent sources agreeing on species/age/girth, freely and publicly accessible, genuinely famous (Slovakia's Tree of the Year 2023 with 4,201 domestic votes, 14th place / 5,204 votes in the 2024 European Tree of the Year contest). Held back from shipping as a Bratislava addition on ONE ground: the real transit time from central Bratislava is too far to read as a day-trip addition to that city page.

verified_facts.location: Zamocky park (Castle Park), Malacky, a National Cultural Monument park attached to the Palffy castle (kastiel). OSM (relation 17436084, leisure=park) gives the park's own bounding box as lat 48.4364-48.4409 / lon 17.0256-17.0369, which the contest page's stated GPS (48.439075, 17.036208) sits inside, corroborating the pin.
verified_facts.species: Pedunculate Oak, Quercus robur. Agreed by every source found (contest page, malacky.sk's own announcement, ekopolis.sk, lesmedium.sk).
verified_facts.age_and_girth: 500+ years, trunk circumference 660cm, height 20m, crown width 31m: these exact figures are repeated identically across the contest page, malacky.sk (the town's own site) and lesmedium.sk (a forestry-industry outlet), which reads as one original measurement (presumably the nomination's own survey) rather than three independent measurements, so treat as one source repeated rather than triangulated; no growth-rate working shown anywhere. Still counts as verified existence/species/rough age under the 'register or documented nomination alone is enough, flagged' standard, given the town council itself (the tree's own municipal owner) is one of the repeating sources.
verified_facts.access: Freely open, no fee, no restriction, confirmed by multiple sources describing the park itself (as opposed to the castle building) as accessible to the public year-round with no time limit ('Park je pristupny verejnosti nepretrzite, bez casoveho obmedzenia'). The adjoining castle building has separate limited opening hours and a small entry fee, but that does not affect the park or the tree, which stands in the open park.
verified_facts.alive_now: Actively promoted by the town's own tourism/municipal channels as of the 2023-2024 contest cycle, with no health concerns mentioned anywhere; good recent evidence of continued life.

leads.why_not_shipped_as_bratislava_addition: Real one-way transit time from central Bratislava is roughly 75-90 minutes door to door: the train from Bratislava hlavna stanica to Malacky takes about 48 minutes on its own (confirmed, hourly ZSSK service), and Malacky's own train station sits about 900m / an 11-13 minute walk from the Castle Park (station at 48.43299,17.02295 per Nominatim, park centre at roughly 48.4386,17.0313). Add getting from central Bratislava to the main station and this clears well past the ~30 minute public-transport day-trip boundary this project uses for a tree to honestly 'belong' on a city page, as opposed to being its own destination reached via Bratislava. The bus is slower still (about 78 minutes). 23.2km straight-line distance already sat at the outer edge of that test; the checked transit time confirms it does not clear the bar.
leads.next_step: Not a research gap, a container decision. Malacky has its own castle and park as a real, small-town destination in its own right, reachable directly from Bratislava by an hourly train; a future pass could consider opening Malacky as its own place under the single-famous-tree / own-destination logic rather than squeezing this oak into Bratislava's day-trip radius. All facts above are already verify-pass complete (sources, pin, access, alive-now) and can be lifted directly.

blocked.name: The Ginkgo of Godrova Street
blocked.place: Godrova 8, predzahradka (the front garden of house No. 8)
blocked.reason:
HARD RULE 10, the half that does not bend. The register's own locality is 'Godrova 8, predzahradka', the FRONT GARDEN of a private house, and the rule names front gardens outright: 'Front gardens, courtyards of dwellings, private houses and their grounds stay out, whatever the register says and however fine the tree. This one does not bend, because the person we would be sending strangers to never asked for any of it.' Verified 2026-08-17 and held by the merging session, not by the verify pass, which delivered it as a view-only entry in good faith.

Why the view-only exception does not rescue it. That exception was written for Hobart's Government House oak, where the REGISTER ITSELF states the tree is 'highly visible as one approaches'. Here the only visibility evidence is a 2011 photograph that appears to have been taken from street level, which is our inference from an image rather than a source's statement, and the rule is explicit that it does not license a tree 'where visible is our guess rather than a source's statement'. Bratislava's published brt_004 is not a precedent either: that one is viewed from a public stairway onto a neighbouring plot, not into somebody's front garden.

What would unblock it: a source that states the tree is visible from Godrova street, or an owner who says visitors may look. The measurements above are good and are kept so a future pass pays nothing to rediscover them.
